synopsis: UN R159 (2021) concerns on-road moving-off information systems that warn truck drivers about pedestrians and cyclists in front of the truck [f5355, f15403, f15389]. The booklet cites its small-cylinder visibility method and tests with road users moving at 3–5 km/h; however, the reported 50 mm cylinder dimension was not confirmed against the regulation text [f5356, f5357, f15404]. Chapter 7 uses the small-cylinder method as an on-road illustration of geometric coverage and blind-zone assessment, an approach supported by expert opinion [f5603, f5604]. The glossary proposes reproducing this method alongside ISO 5006 and ISO 16001 visibility-type methods in each machine’s digital twin before hardware arrives, while Chapter 7 also lists R159 targets among options for ground-truth testing [f15220, f5385].
